title: Sales Positioning and Objection Handling
summary: Learn how to position the STS-1000 after diagnosing procedural turbulence, tailor the value story by buyer role, and respond to common objections without reducing the product to software, AI, or ordinary workflow automation.
llmSummary: This module teaches sales professionals how to position the STS-1000 as a capital infrastructure asset rather than software. It introduces the distinction 'Software observes, automation routes, the STS-1000 stabilizes,' covers buyer-specific messaging for executives, RevOps, IT, Finance, and Compliance, and provides approved responses to objections about workflow software, ERP integration, AI, ROI, capex, consulting, and facilities impact.
objectives: Explain the STS-1000 as a capital infrastructure asset rather than a software platform.
Use the approved distinction: software observes, automation routes, the STS-1000 stabilizes.
Tailor the STS-1000 value story for executives, RevOps, IT, Finance, and Compliance.
Respond to common objections without overexplaining product mechanics.
Avoid language that weakens the product's infrastructure positioning.
Know when to escalate deployment, facilities, power, cooling, or service questions to specialists.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which statement best captures the approved STS-1000 positioning distinction?

answers.text: Software observes, automation routes, and the STS-1000 stabilizes.
Software is outdated, automation is unnecessary, and the STS-1000 replaces all enterprise systems.
The STS-1000 is a dashboard with advanced mechanical styling.
The STS-1000 is primarily an AI assistant for approval workflows.

knowledgeCheck.explanation: The approved distinction is that most enterprise tools observe or route work, while the STS-1000 stabilizes the conditions that allow work to move safely.
